text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia has posted an 11 percent rise in interim profit to A$602 million and an 18 percent increase in dividend, providing a rich reward for its 430,000 shareholders. As a result the bank has cut the new standard variable homeloan rate to 7.55 per cent. Page 1.

Mining group WMC Ltd has seen a sharp slump in first-half profits and dividends as the interim profit fell from A$180.2 million to just A$96.5 million, forcing the group to slash its dividend from 11 cents to six cents. The group is expected to fast track the expansion of its Olympic Dam mine to ease its exposure to the metal-price volatility. Page 17.

Due to a weak advertising market which has cut into its bottom line, Seven Network managing director Gary Rice revealed yesterday the company faces a struggle to meet its earnings targets over coming months, but he says he is optimistic the broadcaster will meet its targets for the next half. Page 17.

Amid strong signs that the Federal Government is likely to try to relax cross-media ownership rules, Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes said yesterday he is reluctantly preparing for changes to the media ownership rules that may allow the broadcasting group to expand into newspapers. Page 17.

Following a redefinition of the exploration area covered by permit WA-74-P, oil and gas group Petroz NL and its wholly owned subsidiary Pontoon NL have followed the lead of joint venture partner WMC Ltd in bringing a compensation claim against the Federal Government over the changes to the permit. Page 19.

Following a panic selling of Helix Resources NL shares on Tuesday, sparked by a disappointing drilling result, which saw Helix shares slumping from A$4.99 to A$3.67, stockbrokers J. B. Were stepped in yesterday with buying support at around A$3.50 in a bid to stabilise Helix's share price. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a result which prompted Commonwealth Bank managing director David Murray to offer an improved forecast for the full year, CBA stunned the market yesterday with a better then expected 11 per cent improvement in its net interim profit from A$542 million to A$602 million for the half-year to December. Page 19.

In a result which reflects lower metal prices, particularly nickel prices, and a strong dollar, WMC Ltd, Australia's third-largest miner, yesterday announced that interim profit had fallen to A$100.7 million from A$186.2 million in the half-year to December. Despite the disappointing result, WMC has committed a further A$230 million to fast-tracking the expansion of its Olympic Dam project. Page 19.

Despite a large increase in the Seven Network's tax bill and soft advertising sales which dragged down interim profit in the half-year to December by 31 percent, Seven chairman Kerry Stokes said yesterday he was happy with the results, which saw pre-tax profit rise by three per cent to a record A$96 million. Page 21.

Thanks to sales increases of between eight and 10 per cent for CSL Ltd's plasma, human vaccine and animal products, the pharmaceutical group has posted a 35 per cent increase in interim net profit to A$12.4 million. Overall sales were lifted five per cent to A$131.5 million for the half-year to December 31. Page 21.

The proposed 740 kilometre, A$383 million Eastern Gas underground Pipeline project, which is a joint venture between BHP Petroleum and Canada's Westcoast Energy, received an environmental green light yesterday from the Victorian Government and is just weeks away from a formal response from the New South Wales Government. Page 21.

As part of its plan to operate flights from Australia to Europe, Melbourne-based airline Australia World Airways said yesterday it has taken over Australian Connection Airlines and issued shares to ACA directors in the hope of winning capacity from Austraia's international air traffic regulator. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Commonwealth Bank stunned the share market with an 11 percent jump in its December half-year profit to A$602 million, pushing CBA shares to an all-time high yesterday. CBA managing director David Murray has revealed the half year result was underpinned by a 17 per cent increase in lending volumes, sound cost management and a 25 percent reduction in the charge for bad and doubtful debts to just A$43 million. Page 31.

Due to weak metal prices and a strong local dollar, coupled with lower production from the 40 per cent-owned Alcoa Worldwide Alumina and Chemicals, WMC yesterday reported a 46 per cent drop in December half-year profit to A$96.5 million after tax and abnomal items. The decline in earnings was at the bottom end of market expectations. Page 31.

The Seven Network's rapid earnings growth has stalled due to a massive jump in income tax and the soft advertising market, with net profit slumping 31.4 per cent from A$91.9 million to A$63 million in the six-month period. Seven had to pay A$34.3 million in income tax compared with just A$0.9 million in the previous corresponding period. Page 31.

Village Roadshow announced yesterday it has successfully raised a A$230 million five-year loan facility from ANZ Bank to help finance its aim of becoming the world's pre-eminent cinema group by 2000. The company said in a statement the money will be mainly used to complete Village Roadshow's planned cinema developments, both in Australia and overseas. Page 33.

In a result CSL managing director Brian McNamee described as pleasing, the blood products and pharmaceutical group announced a 35 percent increase in interim profits yesterday, putting the group on track for further growth in its second half. The A$12.4 illion bottom line surpassed market expectations and fuelled a 28 cent rally in the stock to A$6.07. Page 33.

According to a survey of retirement income stream products released yesterday by industry consultants Rice Kachor Research, the boom in retirement income stream funds management continued last year, with total funds under management on behalf of retirees jumping by 20 per cent to A$14.8 billion. Page 33.
THE AGE

Commonwealth Bank sent shockwaves through the banking sector yesterday, posting an 11 per cent increase in interim profit to A$602 million as investors drove CBA's share price up 50 cents to close at an all time high of A$13.90 and the instalment receipts 46 cents higher to A$9.64. The result added more than A$600 million to the bank's market capitalisation and was way above the most bullish broker forecasts. Page B1.

In a result which WMC managing director Hugh Morgan said yesterday was predictable given lower prices and the higher exchange rate, the mining group recorded a sharp fall in December-half profit from A$186.2 million to A$100.7 million. However, Morgan forecast a marked improvement in the second-half thanks to improved prices, a lower exchange rate, increased production and lower costs. Page B1.

As part of its efforts to devote its attention in the North American packaging industry to plastics, not steel, Southcorp Holdings revealed yesterday it had signed a letter of intent with the United States-based Greif Bros Inc to sell its two steel drum businesses in California and Ontario. Page B3.

Following a string of movie flops, senior executive departures and speculations about its financial woes, Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, the troubled Hollywood studio, has posted an operating revenue of A$302 million and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation ad amortisation of US$16.7 million in its first 12 weeks under the stewardship of the Seven Network and US billionaire Kirk Kerkorian. Page B3.

Village Roadshow announced yesterday it had secured a A$230 million five-year loan facility from ANZ Bank to fund its aggressive expansion program, which Village expects to result in the group operating 550 screen overseas by the end of this financial year and more than 2,300 screens by 2001. Page B3.

Under an arrangement that would effectively amount to a gold deal, Newcrest Mining is believed to have resolved the ongoing question of what it should do with its 12 per cent stake in Normandy Mining by agreeing to a "securitisation deal", which would see Newcrest using the dividends received from Normandy stock to pay interest on the loan. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
